discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 310740
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
340 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- 20% chance for isolated showers or sprinkles today, 
  especially west of I-69. Plenty of dry hours otherwise. 
  Little, if any impacts expected for Halloween evening.

- Very warm on Tuesday followed by increasing rain chances
  through Wednesday (60% chance).

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 337 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

An area of showers is underway spanning from central IA through 
extreme western Indiana. Mesoanalysis shows warm air advection aloft 
along with subtle near-surface convergence, and even modest elevated 
instability (through central IL, fading well before the IN line). 
This WAA and surface convergence lift north-northeast through early 
this afternoon. Despite an 8,000 foot dry layer and a 10-degree dew 
point depression, light rain is underway at Monticello, IN. Trends 
lead me to believe these showers will persist through at least the 
morning hours. The centroid of high pressure is analyzed over the 
greater Lansing area, suggesting the far northeast reaches of these 
showers will be limited, battling additional dry air and subsidence. 
Will carry on with the continued Halloween message of isoalted 
showers mainly west of I-69 (20% chance). Plenty of dry time 
otherwise of Halloween, especially for late-afternoon trick-or-treat 
hours. Cloudy and somewhat cool with highs just beyond 60 degrees. 

Murky, spotty, and weakly forced shower chances linger through at 
least Monday as high pressure gradually gives way to ridging ahead 
of deepening low over the Central US. This results in periods of low-
confidence 20-30% POPs. A weak shortwave moving through the OH River 
Valley presents a 20% chance of showers for far southern reaches of 
the forecast area Sunday afternoon, with perhaps a better moisture 
stream arriving overnight.

The primary item of interest in the extended forecast is the mid- 
latitude cyclone moving through midweek. Very warm on Tuesday (near-
record highs) ahead of this low as the jet stream becomes highly 
amplified over the Midwest. Breezy with southerly wind gusts of 20-
25 mph. The occluding low over far northern lower Michigan looks to 
delay our best rain chance until late Tuesday night and Wednesday. 
How cyclogenesis evolves over the mid-Mississippi thereafter 
dictates how much our rain will see, or whether the cold/occluded 
frontal passage is our only chance for rain. Behind the low, still 
mild for early November with highs in the 60s and lows in the
40s. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...
Issued at 1247 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

Existing TAFs are on track at this time. Wind takes on a more
south-southeasterly direction later this morning at KFWA.
Otherwise, no significant changes. 

An area of rain over southeast IA is poorly modeled this hour.
Mesoanalysis indicates this activity is the result of modest 
850-mb WAA and subsequent theta-e advection, along with a narrow
axis of elevated instability. These features are forecast to 
seep northeast through IL today and will be monitored for 
anything beyond PROB30 -SHRA at KSBN. High confidence in dry 
conditions at KFWA.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Brown

spc.text:
SPC AC 310553

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1253 AM CDT Sat Oct 31 2026

   Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. today or
   tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   A mid-level shortwave trough will move across the central U.S.
   today, as southwesterly flow aloft remains in place over the West.
   At the surface, a large area of high pressure will remain in the
   eastern U.S. as a lee trough develops in the High Plains. Scattered
   thunderstorms will be possible today within a moist airmass in the
   lower Mississippi Valley. Additional storms will be possible in
   parts of the Intermountain West and Upper Midwest. Isolated to
   scattered storms could also form in parts of Arizona and over the
   southern Florida Peninsula. No severe threat is expected today or
   tonight across the continental U.S.

   ..Broyles/Weinman.. 10/31/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 310533

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1233 AM CDT Sat Oct 31 2026

   Valid 011200Z - 021200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM CENTRAL NEW
   MEXICO INTO THE TEXAS PANHANDLE...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few severe storms are anticipated from parts of central New Mexico
   into parts of western Texas late Sunday into Sunday night, with at
   least isolated damaging gusts possible.

   ...Discussion...
   A deep upper trough and low will move quickly across the Great
   Basin, as a southern stream disturbance moves from northern Baja CA
   across AZ during the day and into NM overnight. At the surface, high
   pressure will exist over much of the East, with southerly surface
   winds increasing late in the day and into the overnight from the
   High Plains into the Rockies in advance of the phasing upper system.


   Low pressure will deepen from WY into CO overnight, with a cold
   front moving into western NM late in the day. With the approaching
   upper trough, pre-frontal winds are likely to remain gusty over NM
   into the night which will keep the boundary layer a bit
   warmer/mixed. With 50s F dewpoints, instability should be sufficient
   for at least isolated severe storms as the cold front moves through.
   The RRFS soundings shows around 500 MLCAPE at KABQ between 00-02Z
   preceding the wind shift, with strong shear profiles including 55 kt
   effective shear and effective SRH over 200 m2/s2. Also depicted is a
   high reflectively line with various bowing structures within,
   possibly developing over west-central NM by 00Z. Locally severe
   gusts will be the most likely threat from central NM during the
   evening into eastern NM and the TX Panhandle overnight.

   Depending on how organized any convective line becomes along the
   cold front, some QLCS-type tornado potential could materialize.
   Instability/time of day will be a limiting factor, but a low-end
   threat corridor may become more apparent in later updates.

   ..Jewell.. 10/31/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 310727

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0227 AM CDT Sat Oct 31 2026

   Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
   NORTHERN TEXAS...AND FROM WESTERN AND CENTRAL OKLAHOMA INTO
   SOUTHEAST KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered severe storms may develop across parts of the central to
   southern Plains Monday from late afternoon into the evening, with
   damaging wind gusts the main threat.

   ...Discussion...
   On Monday, a large upper trough will cross the Rockies and move into
   the Plains, with the upper low moving from CO into KS. A leading
   wave will move out of the southern High Plains and into OK/KS during
   the day, while the secondary and stronger wave moves eastward out of
   northern NM.

   At the surface, low pressure will be present over the central High
   Plains Monday morning, and this will deepen into NE by 00Z. A cold
   front will extend southwestward from the low, moving southward
   across CO and western KS during the day. Another front/dryline will
   extend south across central KS, western OK, and western TX through
   00Z, and this boundary will push east overnight as the NM
   disturbance proceeds eastward.

   While ample deep-layer shear and a broad fetch of 60s F dewpoints
   will exist over the central and southern Plains, surface heating
   will be limited over much of the area, and likely relegated to the
   dryline. Forecast soundings indicate a relatively cool but moist
   boundary layer east of the dryline during the day, with a minor
   capping inversion above 850 mb which should prevent warm sector
   storms away from the dryline/front.

   It is therefore anticipated that the severe risk will begin near or
   just after 00Z over western OK and perhaps northwest TX, with
   increasing storm coverage through the evening as activity spreads
   across OK, eastern KS, and parts of northern TX. More isolated
   activity will also be possible along the dryline toward the Rio
   Grande.

   Storms should initiate near the dryline/wind shift where upper 70s F
   temperatures are expected, reducing inhibition. Ample turning with
   height of the wind fields as well as up to a 50 kt low-level jet
   will support storm rotation, whether discrete or forming into a
   line. Instability will not be particularly strong, but sufficient to
   support wind damage, and perhaps a tornado risk between 00-06Z.

   ..Jewell.. 10/31/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0830Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
